Our team

Two physicians and a physician assistant — each with the time to do this well.

All three of our providers are accepting new patients. Each profile below includes training, areas of focus, hospital affiliations, and current availability. If you're not sure who to see, our front desk is happy to match you on the phone.

Dr. Ingrid Westgate

MD · FAAD

Founder & Medical Director

Schedule with Dr. Westgate View availability

Practiced dermatology with the same patients for a decade — and counting.

Dr. Westgate founded Westgate Family Dermatology in 2014 after eight years in a larger group practice in downtown Portland. She built this clinic with one explicit intention: to keep visits unhurried enough to actually do dermatology — listen to the whole story, examine carefully, explain options like the patient is an adult, and follow up like the relationship matters. Ten years later, that's still how she practices.

Her clinical focus is general medical dermatology with a particular interest in complex inflammatory disease (severe atopic dermatitis, refractory psoriasis, granulomatous conditions) and high-risk skin cancer surveillance for patients with prior melanoma, immunosuppression, or significant photodamage. She maintains an active Mohs surgery referral relationship with Dr. Tran-Whitfield and serves as the medical director for the clinic's in-house pathology partnership with OHSU.

Areas of clinical focus

  • Complex atopic dermatitis and severe eczema management, including biologic therapy
  • Psoriasis — topical, phototherapy, and systemic management
  • High-risk skin cancer surveillance and total-body skin examination
  • Inflammatory and granulomatous skin disease (sarcoidosis, granuloma annulare)
  • Pigmentary disorders, including vitiligo and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation

Philosophy of care

"Dermatology is the only specialty where the patient can usually see what we're seeing. That's a gift. It means we get to have real conversations about what we're looking at, why it matters, and what the realistic options are. My job isn't to hand somebody a prescription and a brochure — it's to make sure they leave understanding what's actually going on with their skin and what we're going to do about it together."

"I also believe strongly that good dermatology requires the time to take a thorough history. The same rash on two people can mean two very different things depending on what else is happening in their life — what medications they're on, what they do for work, what they've already tried, how it's affecting their sleep and their day. So we block enough time. That's the trade-off I made when I opened this practice, and I haven't regretted it."

Dr. Marcus Tran-Whitfield

MD · Mohs Surgeon

Surgical Dermatology

Schedule with Dr. Tran-Whitfield View availability

Mohs micrographic surgery, done with the same hands that read the slides.

Dr. Tran-Whitfield joined Westgate Family Dermatology in 2017 after completing his Mohs surgery fellowship at the University of Michigan. He performs Mohs micrographic surgery — a specialized, tissue-sparing technique for removing skin cancers — on three days per week, and sees general dermatology patients on Tuesdays. His Mohs practice handles roughly 600 cases per year, including basal cell carcinomas, squamous cell carcinomas, and selected melanoma in situ on cosmetically sensitive locations.

He completed dual training in dermatology and dermatopathology before pursuing his Mohs fellowship, which means he reads his own frozen-section slides intraoperatively rather than passing them to a separate pathologist. This is the standard of care for fellowship-trained Mohs surgeons and one of the reasons the procedure has such high cure rates.

Areas of clinical focus

  • Mohs micrographic surgery for basal cell and squamous cell carcinoma
  • Excisional surgery for melanoma in situ and select invasive melanoma
  • Reconstruction following skin cancer removal (flaps, grafts, complex closures)
  • High-risk skin cancer surveillance for transplant patients
  • General medical dermatology (Tuesdays only)

Philosophy of care

"Mohs surgery has the highest cure rate of any skin cancer treatment we have — but it's also surgery, and the result lives on someone's face or hand or scalp for the rest of their life. So the goal isn't just 'get the cancer out.' It's 'get the cancer out completely, take as little normal tissue as possible, and reconstruct in a way that heals well and looks like nothing happened.' That requires patience, slow stages when needed, and honest conversations about what the scar will probably look like."

"I trained in dermatopathology before Mohs because I wanted to be the person reading my own slides. When you're the surgeon and the pathologist, there's no handoff and no miscommunication — you know exactly what you're seeing and exactly where it came from in the tissue. That's not better than working with a separate pathologist, but for Mohs surgery specifically, it's how the procedure was designed."

Phoebe Aldarova

PA-C · NCCPA Certified

Physician Assistant — General Dermatology

Schedule with Phoebe View availability

Often the fastest way to get the care you need.

Phoebe joined the practice in 2020 after three years on the dermatology service at a multi-specialty clinic in Salem. As a physician assistant practicing under collaborative agreement with Dr. Westgate, she handles a substantial portion of our general dermatology volume — particularly acne management, eczema follow-ups, pediatric derm visits, and skin checks. Her schedule typically has shorter wait times than the physicians', which makes her an excellent option for patients who need to be seen soon for non-complex concerns.

All of Phoebe's complex cases, biopsies with concerning pathology, and any patient she wants a second opinion on are reviewed with Dr. Westgate — usually the same day. Patients moving between Phoebe and Dr. Westgate within the practice find that the medical record and care plan move with them seamlessly.

Areas of clinical focus

  • Adult and adolescent acne — topicals, oral antibiotics, hormonal management, isotretinoin (with physician oversight)
  • Pediatric dermatology — eczema, warts, molluscum, common rashes, birthmark evaluation
  • Routine skin examinations and benign lesion evaluation
  • Eczema and seborrheic dermatitis follow-up management
  • Cosmetic chemical peels and basic cosmetic consultation

Philosophy of care

"A lot of what brings people into dermatology isn't life-threatening, but it's genuinely affecting their daily life — the acne that's making them dread photos, the eczema that's waking up their kid at 2 a.m., the rash that's been there for months and nobody's been able to explain. Those things deserve careful attention even when they're not 'serious' in the strictest sense. I try to give them that."

"I also really like working with teenagers and young families, because that's a window where good dermatologic care can prevent a lot of long-term scarring — physical and otherwise. Treating someone's acne well in high school is one of the highest-leverage things we do."
